title: Uttar Pradesh voter rolls, 2024 to 2027
shows: s1d labs has read four of Uttar Pradesh's electoral rolls from the Election Commission's PDFs into tables, one file for each of the 403 assembly constituencies: the roll of the 2024 Lok Sabha election, the draft and final rolls of the Special Intensive Revision and the draft roll of the 2027 summary revision. It says it read about 6.8 lakh PDFs, most of them scanned images, with five optical character readers and no language model, and that the 2027 roll, the only one of the four with a text layer, was read directly. By its own count, leaving out entries with a deleted mark, the 2024 roll holds 15,36,26,796 entries, the SIR draft 12,28,31,737, the SIR final 13,11,70,043 and the 2027 draft 13,58,67,928. Its README says that about 4,015 newer parts of the two SIR rolls are missing from its files, which it estimates at about 2.5 million voters in each roll, and it asks readers not to compare its SIR totals with the Commission's state totals until that gap is closed. It reports that a hand check of 402 boxes found every field right in 96.77 per cent of SIR records. In the files it publishes, names, relatives' names, EPIC numbers and house numbers are replaced by keyed-hash tokens, so that one elector can be followed from roll to roll and counted by age and gender, and it says the tokens do not make a record anonymous. It sends the full text to journalists and researchers who apply. It says the Commission's PDFs remain the authority and its counts are not official figures.
quote: The Election Commission's PDFs remain the authority. Our files are a reading of them.
In the public copy a voter keeps the same token in every roll. You can follow one person from 2024 to 2027 and count who left each part, by age and gender, without reading a name.
note: First reading, 24 November 2026, of the page labs.s1d.me/up-eci, dated 24 November 2026 on the page, and of the README of the release (data.s1d.me/eci-rolls/up/README.md), both read on 24 November 2026. The files themselves were not downloaded and the site links only the page, not the downloads, which are row-level tables. Its counts are its own reading of the PDFs, which it says. Set against the Chief Electoral Officer's figures on this site, its 2027 draft of 13,58,67,928 is 977 fewer than the 13,58,68,905 the CEO gave at the press conference of 17 November 2026, and its SIR draft and final counts are each about 2 per cent fewer than the CEO's 12,55,56,025 and 13,39,84,792 (by 27,24,288 and 28,14,749). The README, in a section headed as found on 24 November 2026, says that the part list s1d labs took from the ECI portal for the SIR rolls stops at each constituency's old highest part number, that about 4,015 newer parts in 294 constituencies are therefore missing from both SIR rolls, that it estimates about 2.5 million voters in these parts for each roll (about 2 % of the roll), and that its totals should not be compared with ECI's state totals until the gap is closed. That estimate matches the shortfall against the CEO's figures, and the summary carries the warning. The page also says that both SIR rolls have records for 173,501 of 173,730 parts and that 146 parts of the 2024 roll could not be downloaded. Its 2024 count is not compared, because the site holds no official 2024 figure for the state. The page's own counts reconcile with the README: 12,28,31,737 rows in the SIR draft, 13,11,70,043 plus 6,89,932 with a deleted mark equal to the 13,18,59,975 rows of the SIR final, and 15,36,26,796 plus 32,98,332 equal to the 15,69,25,128 rows of the 2024 roll. The page's word for entries under a DELETED stamp is not used, and the summary gives them as entries with a deleted mark. No change between rolls computed by s1d labs is carried, because the SIR counts differ from the CEO's.
